Reason: The provided image is a bronchoscopic view (not a chest X-ray) showing a small, white foreign body lodged in a bronchus. Among the choices, option B best describes a scenario involving a small foreign body without gross parenchymal collapse (atelectasis) or hyperinflation (air trapping), which aligns with the visual of a discrete object in an otherwise patent-appearing airway and fits the description of a clinically occult aspiration often found via endoscopy despite normal or subtle radiographic findings.
